queue_items.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative carries no rival boundary at all -- it rejects two unit_type labels -- so this six-verse span ships without engagement of any rival cut, including one its own prose points at.
queue_items.grounds: The field rejects forcing the span into wasf_poem or narrative_sequence as a worse fit than lyric_address, and says the span is argued into lyric_address by the closest-fit operative category with the deviation disclosed below. That is a unit_type justification, and the book's operative-category law routes exactly that disclosure to device_notes, where this row already carries it -- so the rival-boundary slot is spent on a duplicate. A rival cut was available from the row's own bytes: MT 3:7-3:10 carry no first- or second-person address form at all (verified -- every suffix across those four verses is third-person), and MT 3:11 then opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte), two 2fp imperatives plus the book's only daughters-of-Zion vocative (sweep: 1 verse), which under the book's voice policy is tier-1 voice-shift evidence standing exactly at the 3:10|3:11 junction. The row's own device_notes concedes the point by saying the addressee shift to the daughters of Zion only surfaces at the closing imperative in Song.3.11, and separately discloses a span-internal setumah at MT 3:8 (single-witness tier-3, correctly non-driving) at the other candidate joint. I am NOT concluding that the shipped span is wrong -- the maximal-run rule and the processional coherence support holding MT 3:6-3:11 whole -- only that the strongest available rival is unengaged, which is a warrant gap on a medium_low row. Not alone load-bearing: both outer edges stand on byte-verified tier-1 anchors. Noted inside the same sentence and folded into this finding rather than scored separately: the phrase closest-fit operative category imports governance vocabulary into row prose.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the unit_type sentence with an actual rival-cut engagement -- reject, or accept and re-span, the 3:10|3:11 cut at the daughters-of-Zion vocative onset, quoting the pointed splice at oshb:Song.3.11 with its tier -- and leave the operative-category deviation disclosure where it already stands in device_notes. Any resulting respan is an adjudication question, not this review's proposal.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The band itself is honest and both outer edges are byte-warranted, so it is neither over- nor under-stated. Front edge: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.3.6) collates byte at its own ref and byte against oshb:Song.8.5, and the ascent-run formula re-sweeps to exactly 2 verses (MT 3:6, MT 8:5) -- the row's sweep-2-verses-at-byte-tier citation is exact. Back edge: MT 4:1 opens the rayati-bound formula argued in the following row. The closing vocative splice צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Song.3.11, tier: byte) is byte-exact and its digit re-sweeps to 1 verse for the daughters-of-Zion form (the daughters-of-Jerusalem substring sweep returns 7 verses only because it catches the MT 3:10 from-phrase, which the row correctly does not count as an address). The three setumot disclosed (MT 3:5 front-seam, MT 3:8, MT 3:11) are all in the WLC inventory, all carried single-witness tier-3, none used as a driver, and the disclosure sweep is complete for the span. The stated reason for the band -- that lyric_address is a closest-fit rather than a literal address-form match across MT 3:6-3:10 -- is true and is properly disclosed in device_notes; frontier_flag_considered is true. The row's real weakness is a field defect recorded separately below, not a mis-set confidence band.

queue_items.claim: The Shulammite uniqueness citation blends two count objects: the in-verse occurrence digit it reports is false for the byte-swept token it names.
queue_items.grounds: The row writes the epithet citation as a single byte-tier object with two digits - 1 verse book-wide and 2 occurrences in-verse. Re-swept with the object named: the byte-tier token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13) returns 1 verse and 1 token occurrence book-wide, not 2. The verse's second epithet token is בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a bet-prefixed form that is a different string at byte tier AND at skeleton tier, and it byte-sweeps to 1 verse / 1 token of its own. The 2-occurrence digit is true only for the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton, which sweeps to 1 verse and 2 token occurrences. The book-wide uniqueness half of the claim is true at either object; the in-verse half is byte-false as cited. Not load-bearing: the seam rests on the fourfold 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) against the 1cs close of oshb:Song.6.12, so the digit corroborates rather than drives.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only (no span effect): re-cut the parenthetical so each digit names its own object and unit - the exact byte-tier epithet token at 1 verse / 1 token book-wide, and, separately labelled, the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton at 1 verse / 2 token occurrences in this verse, naming the bet-prefixed second token as the reason the two objects differ. Retire the blended 'byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse' formulation.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The medium_low band survives the row's own evidence and is honestly reasoned; the digit defect recorded below does not touch it. The front seam is tier-1 twice over: oshb:Song.6.12 closes in 1cs (לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי, byte tier) and oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 opens on the fourfold 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (byte tier) addressed to an epithet found in no other verse of the book (byte sweep of הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית: 1 verse) - an addressee-and-person shift, not a continuity inference. Both residual uncertainties the band reflects are the book's own registered low-confidence items at this verse: the dance-of-Mahanaim construal, and the voice assignment of the מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית clause (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), which the row weighs between the 1cp cohortative with 2fs suffix וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ and the 2mp form תֶּחֱזוּ֙ (both byte tier) without deciding it. The offset-zone dual-cite rule is met on every structured ref touching WEB 6:13 / MT ch 7, and each written dual is arithmetically right (WEB 6:13 = MT 7:1; WEB 7:1 = MT 7:2) - citation validator GREEN, zero offset-zone disclosure problems. The catchword straddle is disclosed rather than suppressed: נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after (skeleton sweep of that catchword: 2 verses book-wide, re-swept and confirmed at MT 6:12 and MT 7:2), and the row's held-open posture is the right response to a device that links the flanking verses across a one-verse span. No tier-4 leaning: the row names the WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus only to disclaim it, and the apparatus site catalogued before WEB 6:13 does no work in the argument.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The seam verse (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1) opens a new exchange against its own front seam: oshb:Song.6.12 closes in first-person singular — לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) — while oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 opens with the repeated 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (byte tier) 'return, return, the Shulammite; return, return', addressed to an epithet unique to this verse (הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית — byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse), an addressee-and-person shift of tier-1 class. The catchword נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after bracket this single-verse span on both seams (skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide). Within the verse the summons is followed by מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) 'why do you gaze at the Shulammite' — WEB “Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?” (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1). Whether the second half is spoken by the same voice as the opening summons is argued from the bytes alone (not from the WEB [SPEAKER] heading), so the call-and-question is held as one exchange rather than split at an unmarked internal line.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row forward into web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2's wasf opening was rejected: the imperative summons and its dance-of-Mahanaim question form a closed rhetorical unit distinct in form from the body-part praise that begins the next verse.

The voice assignment of the mah-tehezu clause is held open between the plural cohortative וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a 1cp form with a 2fs suffix, and the 2mp prefix-conjugation form תֶּחֱזוּ֙ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) in the same clause — evidence weighed on both sides of the plural-speakers-and-feminine-addressee question without deciding it. prev_row.boundary_rationale: A short first-person garden-descent narration, אֶל גִּנַּ֤ת אֱגוֹז֙ יָרַ֔דְתִּי (oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier) 'to the nut-tree grove I went down', WEB “I went down into the nut tree grove” (web:Song.6.11), running into the book's hardest line, לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי מַרְכְּב֖וֹת עַמִּי נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) 'I did not know; my desire/soul set me [with] the chariots of my people, a prince/willing one' — the merkavot-ammi-nadiv crux. No tier-1 marker separates MT 6:11 from MT 6:12 — the same 1cs voice runs through both — so the two verses are held as a single unit even though the speaker's identity and the sense of MT 6:12 are unresolved. The verse immediately preceding this span, MT 6:10, closes the praise unit that precedes it: its third-feminine-singular predication, הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier) 'who looks out', gives way at the seam to the first-person perfect יָרַ֔דְתִּי (oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier) 'I went down' that opens this span — a genuine person-form shift — and MT 6:10 closes under its own setumah division (single-witness) immediately before it.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 6:11 from 6:12 was considered given how sharply MT 6:12 is disputed, but no in-verse voice-shift marker separates the two and the OSHB exegesis note at 6:12 is single-witness apparatus, not a text-level seam.

next_row.boundary_rationale: His wasf of her runs feet to head, byte-matching the derived wasf zone exactly: opening מַה יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2, byte tier) 'how beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince's daughter' and closing מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר בָּרְהָטִֽים (oshb:Song.7.6, byte tier) 'king is held captive in [its] tresses', anarthrous in the Hebrew. WEB opens “How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter!” (web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2) and closes “The king is held captive in its tresses.” (web:Song.7.5 = oshb:Song.7.6). A tier-1 address marker runs across the row's own front seam: the repeated 2fs imperative שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי and the 1cp cohortative with 2fs suffix וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (both oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) address the woman continuously into the row's own opener and its 2fs suffix פְעָמַ֛יִךְ (oshb:Song.7.2, byte tier); only the suffixed-body-part wasf sub-class itself begins at oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, so the front cut still holds on form even though the address does not break there. Every verse in this span sits inside the offset zone: this row's own span is oshb:Song.7.2-Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.1-Song.7.5, so the span-level dual-cite covers the whole run.

queue_items.claim: The exclusivity claim that the wall-noun pair is 'the lexeme's only two sites in the book' is false at the lexeme object it names: the same lexeme's defective-spelled plural stands at MT 5:7.
queue_items.grounds: Re-swept with the object named. At the plene singular SPELLING the row quotes - חוֹמָ֣ה (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) and חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) - the skeleton sweep returns exactly 2 verses (MT 8:9, MT 8:10) and 2 token occurrences, so the digit is right for that spelling. But the row names the count object as 'the lexeme', and the same lexeme's plural stands at oshb:Song.5.7 as שֹׁמְרֵ֖י הַחֹמֽוֹת (byte tier, spliced from the source bytes): written defective, without the vav, it is invisible to any plene sweep - the defective skeleton returns 1 verse (MT 5:7) while the plene plural skeleton returns 0 verses. At the lexeme object the true count is 3 verses (MT 5:7, MT 8:9, MT 8:10), so 'the lexeme's only two sites in the book' is a false exclusivity claim, and it is the book's own mater-lectionis / defective-plene hazard class realised. Not load-bearing: the row states expressly that the seam survives on the in-verse 1cp-to-1cs person change at oshb:Song.8.9|8.10, not on the straddling device the digit decorates.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only (no span effect): re-cut the count object from 'the lexeme' to the attested plene singular spelling, carry the digit as a spelling-scoped sweep (2 verses, MT 8:9 and MT 8:10), and disclose the defective plural at MT 5:7 as the third lexeme site the plene sweep does not reach. Keep the byte / accent_stripped tier labels on the pair as written - they are correct.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The band is well-calibrated and its reason is stated honestly in the row's own prose: the speaker-group identification is disclosed as a content inference rather than a named form, which is the correct posture for a zone the book registers as low-confidence. The seam evidence itself is tier-1 at both edges and byte-true: the 1cp possessive אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) opens against the impersonal gnomic close of MT 8:7, the 1cp verbs נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) carry the same voice through the second verse, and the back seam turns on the in-verse 1cp-to-1cs person change at oshb:Song.8.9|8.10, where אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) opens on a 1cs independent pronoun. The cross-seam straddle is disclosed rather than suppressed, which the book's cohesion rule requires: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) answered by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier); the accent_stripped-tier label on the wall-noun pair is exactly right (byte tier at each ref separately, equal only once cantillation is stripped - re-collated). No tier-4 leaning: the speaker-group label matches a WEB apparatus site but is argued from the 1cp forms and the mother's-sons phrase at oshb:Song.1.6, with the inference disclosed. The two findings below are a count-object defect and a disclosure shortfall; neither disturbs the band, which the row's own evidence supports.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The brothers' deliberation opens with a 1cp possessive, אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) 'a little sister [belongs] to us', marking a new speaker-group distinct from the woman's own 1cs voice throughout the surrounding movements (this achot token is role-split from the bride-epithet achoti used earlier in the book) — the sister here is theirs, not his address to her; the speaker-group identification itself is a content inference rather than a named form, though the keeper-and-vineyard chain at oshb:Song.1.6, בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י (byte tier), the same 'my mother's sons' phrase, links the same group across the book. WEB: “We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister...” (web:Song.8.8). The wall/door conditional in 8:9 continues the same 1cp voice — נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) — as a compact, self-contained mashal, and the immediately preceding verse (web:Song.8.7) closes under a setumah division. The row's own back seam carries a byte-true straddling device: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) is answered clause-for-clause by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) is answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) — the wall-noun חוֹמָ֣ה/חוֹמָ֔ה pair is the lexeme's only two sites in the book, byte tier at each ref, identical only once cantillation is stripped (accent_stripped tier as a pair). The seam nonetheless survives the straddle because the 1cp-to-1cs person change at the oshb:Song.8.9|8.10 boundary is itself in-verse and marked, not because the wall-and-breast answer is absent.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the span to Song.8.8-Song.8.10 as a dialogue_exchange (the brothers' deliberation answered by her wall-and-breasts retort) was considered, but the two verses here are voiced by one speaker-group without an answering party, so this row is held as a self-contained deliberative epigram_unit and the exchange is left to resolve at the next seam.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The love-strong-as-death declaration opens on the ascent question rather than on the seal imperative: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.8.5, skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5) 'who is this coming up from the wilderness', turning within the same verse to second-masculine-singular address, עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ and יְלָדַֽתְךָ (oshb:Song.8.5, byte tier) 'I awakened you' / 'she who bore you' — an intra-verse turn from the third-feminine-singular question to first-person/second-masculine-singular address that is disclosed here rather than resolved. That same 1cs/2ms address chain continues unbroken into the next verse: her imperative שִׂימֵ֨נִי (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) 'set me', addressed to לִבֶּ֗ךָ and זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) 'your heart' and 'your arm', carries the same 2ms suffix as עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ and יְלָדַֽתְךָ — no gendered form changes across the MT 8:5|8:6 join, and no vocative or imperative onset marks a new addressee there, so nothing licenses a cut at it. The span instead opens on the attested oath anchor at its own front seam: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Song.8.4, byte tier) 'I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem', turning the address to the daughters, against which MT 8:5 opens a fresh third-feminine-singular voice on the ascent formula — a genuine speaker turn. WEB: “I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem...” (web:Song.8.4); “Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you.” (web:Song.8.5). The gnomic peak follows without a marked seam, כִּֽי עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) 'for love is strong as death', closing on the divided token pair שַׁלְהֶ֥בֶתְ יָֽה (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier; OSHB divides one WLC word into shalhevet + yah for exegesis, tagging the second element as lemma 3050) — the intensive-suffix-versus-divine-element crux, held rather than decided. WEB: “...a very flame of Yah.” (web:Song.8.6). Verse oshb:Song.8.7 continues the same gnomic claim without a voice-shift marker; the mark layer places no seg between MT 8:4 and MT 8:7, so the span closes on the MT 8:7 seg (single-witness, disclosed as corroboration only), immediately before אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) opens a first-person-plural speaker group at the span's own back edge.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ratifying the cut between MT 8:5 and MT 8:6 on the mood or speech-act change from question to address was the leading rejected alternative: no gendered form changes across that seam and no vocative or imperative onset marks a new addressee there, so the absence of any tier-1 marker at it stands unrebutted. The intra-verse turn inside MT 8:5 itself, from third-feminine-singular question to 1cs/2ms address, is a disclosure duty rather than a boundary, since it occurs within a single verse.

prev_row.device_notes: The shalhevet-yah pair (MT 8:6) is a classic crux (OSHB exegesis note, single-witness apparatus): the construal (intensive 'mighty flame' versus divine element) is held, not decided, and the one-word/divided-token fact is disclosed on this citation; this is the Yah-form surface (sweep: 1 verse) in a book carrying zero plain YHWH/Elohim citations (sweep: 0 of 117 verses, byte-swept). The mi-zot formula at MT 8:5 is the ascent-run member (skeleton sweep: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5), a distinct object from the bare mi-zot interrogative (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) — the two counts are never blended. The span opens on this ascent formula and a 1cs/2ms address chain before it reaches the aphoristic peak at MT 8:6, a deviation from the exemplar epigram shape retained under the same category because no tier-1 marker separates the opening question and address from the peak that follows.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Her retort to the brothers opens on the 1cs pronoun אֲנִ֣י (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), which fixes the speaker as singular against the 1cp נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר of the brothers' oshb:Song.8.9 (byte tier), and the gender-marked forms carrying the attribution itself sit later in the same verse: the feminine-singular participle כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) 'found as one who finds peace', and the 3ms suffix בְעֵינָ֖יו (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) locating the other party as a man. WEB: “I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.” (web:Song.8.10). Her own answer, אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה 'I am a wall', answers their wall/door hypothetical with a concrete self-claim rather than a general maxim, and וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת answers their וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ from oshb:Song.8.8 (both byte tier).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this verse as a continuation of the brothers' 1cp deliberation was rejected: the 1cs pronoun ani marks a clean return to her own voice, matching the book's other ani-texture sites.
